_note: The programme, bundled into the app shell so anvil is usable on first open with no token and no network. Structure and coaching cues only: this repo is public and never carries real logged data, loads, or personal health details. The live copy lives in the private data repo and keeps every logged session and baseline. Block 1 (Crystal Life/Training-Recipe), committed 2026-10-11. programVersion decides which split wins: when it differs from the private data repo's, the app adopts this one and writes it back.

exercises.name: Incline DB Press
exercises.cue: Bench at 30 degrees, shoulder blades pinned, lower to chest level for the stretch, press up and slightly in.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.cue: Handles at mid-chest, full stretch at the back, shoulders stay back at the top.

exercises.name: Cable Fly or Pec Deck
exercises.effort: last set to failure, then half reps at the stretch
exercises.cue: Arms softly bent and locked there, open wide until the chest stretches, hug back in.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.effort: last set to failure, then half reps at the stretch
exercises.cue: Stand tall or lean 10-15 degrees, arms 30 degrees in front, lead with the elbows to shoulder height, no shrug.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.cue: Elbows up and in, lower deep behind the head for the stretch, extend fully.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.cue: Side-on to the cable, handle at the chest, press straight out and hold 2 seconds while it tries to twist you.

exercises.name: Cable Row
exercises.cue: Chest up, let the weight pull the shoulders forward for the stretch, row to the lower ribs, torso still.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-up or Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Dead hang at the bottom every rep, chest to the bar. Bodyweight logs as 0.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported High Row
exercises.cue: Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral High Row: chest on the pad, let the shoulders rise for the stretch, pull down and back.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.cue: Rope at forehead height, pull to the eyes, hands finish beside the ears, thumbs back.

exercises.name: Cable External Rotation
exercises.cue: Elbow pinned to the side (towel under the arm), rotate the forearm outward, slow back.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Neutral grip, elbows still, all the way down each rep.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.cue: Curl the pelvis up, knees toward the chest, tailbone tucks. No swinging.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.effort: stop 2 reps short, never to failure
exercises.cue: High bar, brace first, sit down between the heels as deep as you stay tight, drive up fast.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Back foot on the bench, front knee roughly over the toes, drop straight down.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Extension
exercises.effort: last set to failure, then half reps at the stretch
exercises.cue: Knee lined up with the pivot, pause 1 second at the top, control down. One leg at a time.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.cue: Lean the torso forward: more hamstring stretch, more growth.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.cue: Feet mid-platform, shoulder width, lower until the hips just start to curl off the pad.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.cue: High to low across the body, turn through hips and upper back together, arms long.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.cue: Seated DB: bench upright or one notch back, start at ear height, press up and slightly in, no big arch.

exercises.name: Flat Bench Press
exercises.cue: Shoulder blades pinned, touch the lower chest, press back toward the face. Bar or DBs.

_tiers: P3. Every session has three versions and all of them advance the rotation. An exercise's `tier` is the LOWEST tier it survives to: 3 = the one movement that still counts as having trained, 2 = the main work, 1 = accessory. Tier N shows every exercise with tier >= N. A tier 3 day is a completed day; the alternative to tier 3 is not tier 1, it is nothing.

sat.name: Tennis, or a run
sat.work: Tennis, any length, or a 25 to 30 min outdoor run at a conversational pace (65 to 75 percent of max heart rate).
sat.recovery: None, it is one continuous effort.
sat.when: Later in the day, at least 6 hours after the lift.
sat.why: One session a week to start, because three a week were written and none happened. It sits two days clear of both lower days. A second session is added only once this one happens most weeks.

conditioning.watchRule: Apple Watch Cardio Fitness updates ONLY from Outdoor Walk, Outdoor Run and Outdoor Hike. Treadmill, gym and indoor interval work never move the number no matter how hard it was. The run is marked outdoor for exactly this reason: a whole training block reads as a flat line otherwise, which looks like a stalled programme when the opposite is true.

_conditioningRest: Cut to ONE session a week on 2026-10-12 (Anvil decision 0011, tenet 4: attendance before perfection): three a week were written and none happened. The 2026-08-24 prescription (two Zone 2 runs plus one interval block, 120 to 150 aerobic minutes a week) is in git history and is the target to grow back toward once one session a week is routine. The session stays later in the day, at least 6 hours after the lift, because the explosive-strength cost of concurrent training is concentrated when cardio and lifting share a session.
_scheduleNote: Six-day A/B push/pull/legs, completion-based: the weekday keys only fix the ORDER of the queue. Block 1 runs 2026-10-11 to 2026-12-05, deload 2026-12-07 to 2026-12-13. Log the top set only.
_quality: Pre-lift quality work, from the owner's Training-Rebuild plan, ratified 2026-08-24. It runs AFTER the warm-up and BEFORE the lifting, fresh, because explosive qualities are the first thing fatigue erases. It is NOT counted as working sets and never enters the double progression: this is rate of force development, not volume. Plyometric doses are NSCA coaching convention rather than meta-analytic, and are labelled as such.

mon.name: Plyometrics
mon.work: Pogo hops, low box jumps, broad jumps. 40 to 60 foot contacts total.
mon.fallback: Pogo hops and broad jumps only, 30 contacts.
mon.cue: Step DOWN off the box, never jump down. Quality over count, and stop the moment ground contact starts getting slow.
mon.why: Novice dose is 50 to 80 contacts, 1 to 2 sessions a week, 48 to 72 hours apart. Weeks 1 to 3 start at 40 to 60 and progress no more than 10 to 20 percent a week. NSCA coaching convention, not meta-analytic.

tue.name: Jump rope
tue.work: 3 minutes, easy, unbroken if you can.
tue.cue: Stiff ankles, quiet feet, minimal knee bend.
tue.why: Leg stiffness is what lets a player leave the ground later on the split step and still recover. Counts at roughly a third value toward plyometric contacts.

wed.work: 3 minutes, easy, unbroken if you can.
wed.cue: Stiff ankles, quiet feet, minimal knee bend.
wed.why: Leg stiffness is what lets a player leave the ground later on the split step and still recover. Counts at roughly a third value toward plyometric contacts.

thu.name: Sprints and change of direction
thu.work: 6 to 8 x 25 m at 90 to 95 percent, walk back, 60 to 90 s. Then 5-10-5 shuttle x 6.
thu.cue: Short reps keep the fatigue cost near zero. If the times fall off, you are done.
thu.why: The purest fast-twitch stimulus and the cheapest in fatigue, as long as the reps stay short. Skip the shuttle on a tennis day, tennis already supplies plenty of change of direction.

fri.name: Med ball
fri.work: Rotational scoop throws 3 x 5 each side, overhead slams 3 x 5.
fri.cue: Throw it hard. Do not grind it, this is speed work.
fri.why: Low load, high speed, which is exactly why it suits a cranky shoulder. It is also the transverse plane that nothing else in the week trains.

restDay.name: Rest
restDay.job: One easy 20 to 30 minute walk or jog, OR 20 minutes of mobility on ankle dorsiflexion and the shoulder. Pick one, or neither.
restDay.why: No alarm. This day exists to pay the sleep debt: you get 6 to 7 hours against a 7.5 to 8 target while waking early six mornings, and restricted sleep measurably cuts myofibrillar protein synthesis. The tiny job is an adherence device, not training. An unscheduled day is where a six-day habit breaks, so day seven gets a named job precisely to protect the other six.
restDay.notRest: Tennis and bouldering are not rest, and they belong on lifting days.

commute.push: Jog to the gym, easy, capped at about 10 minutes.
commute.pull: Jog to the gym, easy, capped at about 10 minutes.
commute.lower: Walk or bike. Never jog in before squats or deadlifts.
commute.why: Prior aerobic work degrades the lifting that follows, the impairment is localised to the muscles you just used, and it scales with volume. Under about 10 minutes easy is a general warm-up and costs nothing. Twenty to thirty minutes before squats is a leg pre-fatigue protocol wearing a warm-up costume.
